title: The Qbar-l category is idempotent complete
statement:
The category $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is idempotent complete, and the canonical fully
faithful functor $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)\to\Kar(\Dbc(T,\Qlb))$ is an exact
equivalence.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this form: the ledger's
verified entries contain no idempotent-completion entry, and the blueprint
adds the idempotent completeness of the $\Qlb$ category together with the
equivalence of its Karoubi envelope, deduced from the filtered retract
descent and the Karoubianity of the finite-stage categories. The nearest
entries, each fetched and quoted, are the Karoubianity criteria Lemma 12.4.2
([Tag 09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH)) and Lemma 12.4.3
([Tag 05QV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QV)) with Lemma 13.4.14
([Tag 05QW](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QW), a triangulated
category with countable products, or with countable coproducts, is
Karoubian); Stacks defines no Karoubi envelope and no idempotent completion,
and the request to add the envelope stands as a comment on Homological
Algebra, Section 12.4 ([Tag
09SF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SF)). Difference: the
hypothesis here is not countable products or coproducts but idempotent
completeness of every finite stage, and the conclusion concerns a filtered
colimit of coefficient categories.

proof.text: Fix exactly the prime, algebraic closure and scheme hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]: $T$ is noetherian of finite dimension and $\ell$ is invertible on $T$. Its category $\mathcal P_T$ is the pair category of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], with stages the raw rational categories $\mathcal C_E(T)=\Dbc(T,E)$, not their formally adjoined retracts. For every finite intermediate coefficient field $E$, [thm-weil-pbc-finite-stage-karoubian] says that this very $\Dbc(T,E)$ is idempotent complete. These are precisely the hypotheses of the current [prop-weil-filtered-retract-descent]; its conclusion gives that every idempotent $e:X\to X$ of $\mathcal P_T$ has a splitting $i:S\to X$, $p:X\to S$ with $p\circ i=\operatorname{id}_S$ and $i\circ p=e$, and that the splitting may be represented over one finite coefficient field. Thus $\mathcal P_T$ is idempotent complete.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: finite-stage Karoubianity and filtered retract descent.

proof.text: Write $J:\mathcal P_T\to\Kar(\mathcal P_T)$ for the canonical functor $X\mapsto(X,\operatorname{id}_X)$ of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. The category $\mathcal P_T$ is additive, since [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms] makes it an ordinary triangulated category. Apply the current [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-fully-faithful], whose hypothesis is exactly that the input category is additive: $J$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Proof, second sentence: full faithfulness of the canonical functor.

proof.text: For any $Q=(X,e)$ of the envelope of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope], take a splitting $(S,i,p)$ supplied by step 1. In ordinary right-to-left composition, $e\circ i=i\circ p\circ i=i$ and $p\circ e=p\circ i\circ p=p$. Hence $i$ is an envelope morphism $J(S)\to Q$ and $p$ an envelope morphism $Q\to J(S)$. Their composites are $p\circ i=\operatorname{id}_S$, the identity of $J(S)$, and $i\circ p=e$, the identity of $Q$. Thus they exhibit $J(S)\cong Q$. This proves essential surjectivity directly from the two splitting equations.

source.place: Proof, middle sentences: the splitting gives an isomorphism to an object in the image.

proof.text: Here is the equivalence data, without an additional equivalence criterion. For each $Q=(X,e)$ choose a splitting $(S_Q,i_Q,p_Q)$ as above, choosing the trivial splitting $S_{J(X)}=X$, $i_{J(X)}=p_{J(X)}=\operatorname{id}_X$ for identity idempotents. Define $G(Q)=S_Q$ and $G(u)=p_R\circ u\circ i_Q$ for an envelope morphism $u:Q\to R=(Y,d)$. By the morphism condition in [def-weil-karoubi-envelope], $u=d\circ u\circ e$, so $d\circ u=d^2\circ u\circ e=d\circ u\circ e=u$ and $u\circ e=d\circ u\circ e^2=d\circ u\circ e=u$. Thus $G(\operatorname{id}_Q)=p_Q\circ e\circ i_Q=\operatorname{id}_{S_Q}$ and, for $v:R\to U$, $G(v)\circ G(u)=p_U\circ v\circ d\circ u\circ i_Q=G(v\circ u)$. This defines a functor with $GJ=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal P_T}$. The maps $i_Q:JG(Q)\to Q$ and $p_Q$ are mutually inverse by step 3 and are natural: $i_R\circ JG(u)=d\circ u\circ i_Q=u\circ i_Q$. For the inverse, $JG(u)\circ p_Q=p_R\circ u\circ i_Q\circ p_Q=p_R\circ u\circ e=p_R\circ u$, so the maps $p_Q$ are natural too. They give a natural isomorphism $JG\cong\operatorname{id}_{\Kar(\mathcal P_T)}$. Its component at $J(X)$ is the identity, and $G(i_Q)=p_Q\circ i_Q=\operatorname{id}_{S_Q}$, so the triangle identities with the identity unit also hold. Consequently $J$ and $G$ are an equivalence. The quasi-inverse is additive as well: $G(u+v)=p_R\circ(u+v)\circ i_Q=p_R\circ u\circ i_Q+p_R\circ v\circ i_Q=G(u)+G(v)$ and $G(0)=0$, by bilinearity in the additive category $\mathcal P_T$.

source.place: Proof, consequence of essential surjectivity: explicit quasi-inverse, functor laws, counit and triangle identities.

proof.text: By [thm-weil-pbc-verdier-axioms], the particular common-stage shift and cone triangles on $\mathcal P_T$ form an ordinary triangulated category. Therefore [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-triangulated] applies to $\mathcal T=\mathcal P_T$: its envelope has the shift $(X,e)[1]=(X[1],e[1])$ and the retract triangulation, and the canonical functor $J$ is exact. Here exactness has precisely the shift-compatible distinguished-triangle meaning of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Combining this exactness with the equivalence of step 4 proves the asserted exact equivalence.

source.place: Proof, final clause: canonical exactness for the envelope of this triangulated category.

blueprint_update.statement:
The category $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)=\mathcal P_T$ of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] is idempotent complete, and the canonical fully
faithful functor $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)\to\Kar(\Dbc(T,\Qlb))$ is an exact
equivalence.

proof.text:
By [thm-weil-pbc-finite-stage-karoubian] every finite-stage category
$\Dbc(T,E)$ is idempotent complete, so [prop-weil-filtered-retract-descent]
applies with $\mathcal P_T=\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$, as defined in
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]: every idempotent of $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ splits. The
canonical functor into the Karoubi envelope is fully faithful, and it is
essentially surjective: an object $((E,K),e)$ of the envelope is split by
the splitting of $e$ in $\mathcal P_T$ (the idempotent completeness just
proved), say by $K'\in\mathcal P_T$, $i:K'\to(E,K)$, $p:(E,K)\to K'$ with
$p\,i=\operatorname{id}$ and $i\,p=e$, and then $i$ and $p$ exhibit the
isomorphism $((E,K),e)\cong(K',\operatorname{id}_{K'})$ of the envelope (the
Karoubi-morphism conditions $p=p\circ e$ and $i=e\circ i$ follow from
$p\,i=\operatorname{id}$ and $i\,p=e$). Hence the functor is essentially
surjective, and exact because the envelope of a triangulated category is
triangulated with the canonical functor exact.
